instruction.text: This is a map showing the continents of the world. Select the image that shows North America.

atoms.b: North ((++America Africa)) is made up of 23 countries, with a population of around 621 million people.
North America is bordered by the Atlantic Ocean in the east, the Pacific Ocean to the west and the Arctic Ocean to the ((++north south)).
Canada is the ((++largest smallest)) country in North America, taking up nearly half of the continent by area.
The ((++smallest largest)) country in North America is Saint Kitts and Nevis, which is located in the Caribbean.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

hint.label: Imaginary lines
hint.text: The Arctic Circle and the Tropic of Cancer are imaginary lines circling the Earth. The Arctic Circle marks the Earth’s northernmost region, whereas the Tropic of Cancer is located just north of the Equator.

atoms.text: North America has a very diverse climate because of its size. Different regions experience different types of climates, and they change drastically from north to south.
Parts of Northern Canada and Alaska have polar climates with very cold winters and permanently frozen ground.
In Southern Canada and most of the United States, the climate is temperate, with moderate temperatures and regular rainfall throughout the year.
In the south of the USA and Northern Mexico, the climate is hot and dry with rugged deserts and little rainfall.
Southern Mexico, Central America and the Caribbean have tropical climates, which are hot and humid with lots of rainfall and even hurricanes!

What sort of climate does Alaska have?

sound.end: Pond Inlet has a polar climate.
Monttego Bay has a tropical climate.

atoms.b: Canada, the USA and Mexico take up the vast ((++majority minority)) of North America. The USA alone is almost the exact size of the entire European continent!
As they are so ((++large small)), all three of these countries use federal systems, where power is divided between a national government and regional governments.
For example, the USA has 50 states, each with their own ((++government president)), which make decisions for the people living there on things like education and local roads.
The US national government in ((++Washington,_D.C. London)) then makes decisions for the whole country on bigger things, such as defence and foreign policy.
